market_summary: The pre-market setup is constructive but selective, based on 1938 articles from Yahoo Finance, simplywall.st, AOL.com, Investing.com, 24/7 Wall St.. The dominant theme is company, with 673 macro items, 679 company items, 508 industry items, and 78 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
macro_summary: Late Cycle Markets are balancing easier policy expectations against growth and earnings risk, keeping leadership narrow and confirmation dependent. The market is taking its direction from oil/energy, with investors testing whether policy support can offset slower growth and earnings risk. Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (182), inflation (121), oil/energy (107), growth/jobs (26). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_summary: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 353 positive, 223 negative, and 1362 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
